definitions.explanation: HKCC is the predefined view of the current hardware profile. It aliases HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Hardware Profiles\Current. Its purpose is to expose profile-specific differences from the standard machine configuration. Interpret this root as an access view: the same configuration may appear under its full machine path, and this name alone does not identify a physical device or a changed setting.

research.summary: HKCC is the predefined view of the current hardware profile.
research.log_context: A record naming HKCC concerns the current hardware-profile view; retain the resolved full path, requested operation and process context.
cannot_infer: The root does not identify a particular device.
A reference through HKCC and its machine alias need not represent two changes.
research.applicability: Hardware profiles are deprecated in current driver guidance; this alias remains documented.

evidence.claim: HKCC aliases the current hardware-profile branch.

definitions.explanation: HKCR exposes a merged view of machine and current-user class registrations. The backing branches are HKLM\Software\Classes and HKCU\Software\Classes. File associations and COM metadata are interpreted through that view, whose result depends on user and process context. A record using HKCR must therefore preserve the originating security context and registry view before attributing the data to a machine-wide or per-user registration.

research.summary: HKCR exposes a merged view of machine and current-user class registrations.
research.log_context: For a COM or file-association registry event, resolve the backing hive and retain user SID, process architecture, value name and operation.
cannot_infer: HKCR is not an independent hive with a single backing store.
Registration metadata does not establish that a component executed.
research.applicability: Merge behavior and COM use depend on user context, elevation and Windows compatibility rules described in the source.

evidence.claim: HKCR merges machine and user Classes data.

definitions.explanation: HKCU provides access to the registry settings associated with the current user context. The handle maps to a branch under HKEY_USERS and exposes preferences such as application settings and environment configuration. It should be interpreted with the process security context, especially for services and impersonation. The root alone identifies neither the human who initiated an event nor a particular application preference.

research.summary: HKCU provides access to the registry settings associated with the current user context.
research.log_context: A log reference to HKCU needs the process identity, user SID and full descendant path to establish whose settings were accessed.
cannot_infer: The same HKCU text in different processes need not identify the same user hive.
A user-profile reference does not prove interactive user activity.
research.applicability: The predefined-handle mapping is established per process; impersonating services should use the documented user-specific APIs.

evidence.claim: HKCU maps to a user branch in HKEY_USERS.

definitions.explanation: HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (HKLM) is the predefined root for configuration associated with the local computer. Its subtrees separate operating-system configuration, software settings, hardware information, and security-related configuration. This layer establishes machine scope; it does not select a particular user profile or identify the operation performed on a descendant key.

research.summary: HKLM identifies configuration associated with the local computer.
research.log_context: An HKLM record establishes machine scope; operation, full child path and value data are still required to identify the affected facility.
cannot_infer: Machine scope does not identify the process that performed an operation.
The root does not imply every contained component is enabled.
research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: LocalMachine accesses HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE configuration.

definitions.explanation: HARDWARE contains hardware and driver-mapping information rebuilt during system startup. It is a machine branch with descriptive and resource-oriented descendants, distinct from persistent service configuration. Treat observations as information from a particular boot context. A change between two snapshots can reflect rediscovery or driver initialization, so attribution requires the surrounding boot and device timeline rather than a path comparison alone.

research.summary: HARDWARE contains hardware and driver-mapping information rebuilt during system startup.
research.log_context: Hardware records should retain boot/session time, full key, value data and the querying or writing process.
cannot_infer: The branch is not a durable history of every attached device.
A snapshot difference does not by itself prove a hardware replacement.
research.applicability: The documentation describes Windows hardware registry organization; driver-class formats and enumerated content vary.

evidence.claim: HARDWARE data is recreated at startup.

definitions.explanation: DESCRIPTION holds descriptive information about the computer hardware. Under the volatile HARDWARE branch, this node narrows an observation to hardware description rather than service-start settings or resource claims. The actual component and property are identified only by descendants and values. Use this as a descriptive namespace in a knowledge graph, without assigning a particular processor, bus or firmware characteristic to the parent.

research.summary: DESCRIPTION holds descriptive information about the computer hardware.
research.log_context: A hardware-description event needs the complete descendant path and value payload to identify the component property.
cannot_infer: The parent does not establish a particular processor or firmware version.
The namespace is not a complete historical hardware inventory.
research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: Description describes actual computer hardware.

definitions.explanation: DEVICEMAP groups hardware mapping data whose layout depends on the driver class. Its position under HARDWARE distinguishes the mappings from the persistent registration of a service under SYSTEM. Different children can represent different device classes, so the parent has no universal value schema. An analyst must resolve the child class and consult its contract before interpreting the data as a device identifier or driver association.

research.summary: DEVICEMAP groups hardware mapping data whose layout depends on the driver class.
research.log_context: A device-mapping record requires its class-specific child path, value name, data type and boot context.
cannot_infer: No universal value schema can be assigned to this parent.
A mapping alone does not demonstrate successful device I/O.
research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: DeviceMap data formats are driver-class-specific.

definitions.explanation: VIDEO is a video-related child within the hardware device-mapping namespace. Microsoft uses this exact branch to illustrate how keys differ from values in the registry. research.summary: VIDEO is a video-related child within the hardware device-mapping namespace.
research.log_context: A VIDEO mapping event needs the exact value name and display-driver context; the prefix alone only locates the mapping area.

research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: VIDEO is a DEVICEMAP child; MaxObjectNumber and VgaCompatible are example values.

definitions.explanation: RESOURCEMAP describes hardware resources claimed by device drivers. This branch belongs to the startup-recreated HARDWARE tree. It supplies context for interpreting resource-related observations, but a particular claim belongs to a specific descendant and its data. Distinguish the registry description of resource use from an observed conflict or operational failure, which requires additional device and driver evidence.

research.summary: RESOURCEMAP describes hardware resources claimed by device drivers.
research.log_context: Resource-map events require the driver-specific path, resource data and boot context to identify the claimed resource.
cannot_infer: The parent does not prove a resource conflict.
A recorded claim does not show successful access to the resource.
research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: ResourceMap describes driver claims on hardware resources.

definitions.explanation: SAM is the machine hive associated with Security Accounts Manager account information. It is a separate top-level branch from SECURITY and from per-user preference hives. This node should identify the account-database area without assigning a particular account, password representation or administrative action to the prefix. A registry record here needs an exact descendant and access result before its subject or consequence can be described.

research.summary: SAM is the machine hive associated with Security Accounts Manager account information.
research.log_context: For SAM access, preserve the descendant, requested rights, result, process and account identity; distinguish successful reads from denied attempts.
cannot_infer: The root does not identify an affected account.

evidence.claim: SAM is the account-security database branch.

definitions.explanation: SECURITY is the machine hive containing local security-policy information. It is separate from the SAM account database and from ordinary application settings. The containing hive provides a useful security-configuration context but does not expose a particular policy decision at this level. Interpret a recorded access using the target descendant and access outcome, rather than assuming that every reference changes permissions or reveals protected data.

research.summary: SECURITY is the machine hive containing local security-policy information.
research.log_context: A SECURITY event requires the exact descendant, operation, result and process identity to distinguish policy inspection from an effective change.
cannot_infer: The hive name does not identify a specific granted user right.

evidence.claim: Security is a distinct hive described as local security-policy storage.

definitions.explanation: SOFTWARE contains configuration and registration data for software on the computer. This branch establishes machine scope while leaving the owner and feature to descendant keys. It includes several independent namespaces, so the same value name can carry different meanings below different products. A knowledge lookup should continue down the full path before assigning application behavior, installation state or policy meaning to an observation.

research.summary: SOFTWARE contains configuration and registration data for software on the computer.
research.log_context: A SOFTWARE event needs the vendor/product path, registry view and value data to identify the affected setting.
cannot_infer: The parent does not identify an installed application.

research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: Software is the per-computer software database.

definitions.explanation: Classes holds the machine contribution to file associations and COM registration. It supplies default registration data that can participate in the HKCR merged view. This explicit machine location is useful when distinguishing per-computer registration from user overrides. Interpret an observed registration together with the relevant extension, ProgID, class or interface identifier; this parent alone selects no executable and supplies no execution evidence.

definitions.explanation: A FileExtension child associates a file-name suffix with a programmatic identifier. The placeholder represents the shape of an extension registration, such as a name beginning with a period, rather than a discovered extension on a host. The association is metadata for resolving a file class. It neither contains a file nor records the opening of one, and downstream interpretation needs the concrete suffix and associated identifier.

research.summary: A FileExtension child associates a file-name suffix with a programmatic identifier.
research.log_context: For an extension-association change, retain the actual extension, unnamed value data, process and registry view.
cannot_infer: The placeholder does not prove any concrete extension exists.
An association change does not prove a document was opened.

Shell registrations describe how an application handles a file type; COM-oriented registrations can associate the name with a CLSID. These uses must not be conflated: a file-association ProgID does not by itself establish a COM mapping. Resolve the actual child entries before assigning a class identity, handler command or application behavior.

definitions.explanation: AppID groups application-level COM configuration registrations. Its GUID-named children can collect settings shared by multiple DCOM classes. The parent therefore represents a registration namespace rather than one executable or security policy. To interpret an observation, resolve the application identifier and the specific setting below it; do not copy a child application identity or launch rule onto the entire branch.

research.summary: AppID groups application-level COM configuration registrations.
research.log_context: An AppID namespace event needs the actual GUID child and value operation before identifying a DCOM configuration change.
cannot_infer: The parent does not designate one executable.
Its existence does not prove remote activation is enabled.
research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: AppID registrations centralize settings for DCOM objects.

definitions.explanation: An AppID GUID child holds configuration shared by the COM classes associated with that application identity. Class-to-AppID association is separate from both the GUID name and runtime activation. A log interpretation needs the concrete identifier and changed value to distinguish an identity mapping from a permissions or hosting modification.

research.summary: An AppID GUID child holds configuration shared by the COM classes associated with that application identity.

definitions.explanation: CLSID organizes machine COM registrations by class identifier. A child GUID names one class-registration record; the parent is a collection rather than a particular COM implementation. Server paths and other activation-related metadata belong beneath individual class entries. Keep the concrete class identifier when analyzing a record so that registrations for unrelated components are not collapsed into a single behavior.

cannot_infer: The collection does not identify a server binary.

evidence.claim: Class registrations are arranged beneath CLSID by class GUID.

definitions.explanation: A CLSID child is the registration record for one COM class identity. The identifier selects a class, while descendants describe its server and related metadata. The inventory placeholder is a schema location, not a known GUID on the examined computer. To interpret a log entry, connect the concrete class to the exact modified registration and preserve architecture and user context before drawing activation conclusions.

research.summary: A CLSID child is the registration record for one COM class identity.

definitions.explanation: InprocServer32 describes the in-process server registration for a COM class. Its unnamed value identifies the server path and ThreadingModel supplies apartment-related metadata. This fixed child remains dependent on a concrete parent CLSID. A registry write changes registration data; confirming a load requires separate module or activation evidence, including the process architecture and the effective registration view used by the client.

research.summary: InprocServer32 describes the in-process server registration for a COM class.

evidence.claim: InprocServer32 contains a server path and ThreadingModel.

definitions.explanation: LocalServer32 identifies a local executable COM server registration for a class. Despite its historical name, Microsoft documents server applications of any bitness or architecture. The unnamed value can include arguments, and ServerExecutable can disambiguate the executable. These are activation inputs rather than process history; a registry observation needs the concrete CLSID and value data before it can describe a server-registration change.

research.summary: LocalServer32 identifies a local executable COM server registration for a class.

definitions.explanation: Interface groups COM interface registrations by interface identifier. The parent separates interface metadata from COM class registrations. definitions.explanation: HKU\.DEFAULT is the LocalSystem profile branch, not the template for newly created users. Microsoft identifies it with the LocalSystem account and its S-1-5-18 profile alias. The misleading name must not be used to infer that edits propagate to every future user. For event interpretation, associate the path with system-account profile settings and inspect the actual descendant before identifying a logon-interface or service preference.

research.summary: HKU\.DEFAULT is the LocalSystem profile branch, not the template for newly created users.
research.log_context: A .DEFAULT event needs the precise setting and process identity; it may concern system-account profile use rather than a human user preference.
cannot_infer: A write here does not establish a change to the new-user Default profile template.
The path alone does not establish that the logon UI used the changed setting.
research.applicability: The Microsoft developer explanation is historical; its XP file paths and deployment instructions are not generalized to modern systems.

evidence.claim: The .Default profile belongs to LocalSystem and is not the new-user template.

definitions.explanation: A UserHive child represents a loaded user-profile registry context. The placeholder is an identity slot, not a literal SID or a guarantee that a particular account is signed in. Environment and software settings below it belong to the resolved hive context. A log interpretation must bind the actual child name using account or hive-loading evidence, while keeping user identity separate from the process that accessed the data.

research.summary: A UserHive child represents a loaded user-profile registry context.
research.log_context: Retain the concrete hive identifier, resolved account and accessing process; an accessing process can differ from the profile owner.
cannot_infer: The placeholder does not prove that an account or loaded hive exists.
A hive owner is not necessarily the actor who accessed its settings.
research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: HKEY_USERS contains per-user profile hives.

definitions.explanation: Environment stores persistent environment-variable definitions for the selected user hive. This node is scoped by the actual UserHive ancestor and is distinct from machine environment configuration under Session Manager. A value change updates stored profile configuration, while a process has its own effective environment. To explain an event, retain the variable name and data and establish which user hive and process lifetime are involved.

research.summary: Environment stores persistent environment-variable definitions for the selected user hive.
research.log_context: A user-environment event needs the concrete hive identity, variable name, data and process creation context.
cannot_infer: The template does not identify the current interactive user.
A write does not prove an already running process adopted the new value.

value_semantics.name: Variable-name entries
value_semantics.meaning: Named entries define persistent environment variables for this user hive.

evidence.claim: Win32_Environment queries per-user variables from this path.

definitions.explanation: Software is the application-configuration namespace within a selected user hive. It sits below the profile identity and above vendor or product branches, so its scope is broader than Microsoft settings or certificate storage. The verified SystemCertificates descendant supports this containing path. Preserve the concrete hive and software owner before interpreting a record as a change to one application preference.

research.summary: Software is the application-configuration namespace within a selected user hive.
research.log_context: An event here locates software configuration for the resolved hive owner. The vendor/product child and value data are needed to identify which application setting was involved.
cannot_infer: The ancestor does not identify a specific certificate or store.
The placeholder does not prove a particular user profile is loaded.
research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: The documented per-user certificate path establishes this ancestor.

definitions.explanation: Microsoft selects a vendor grouping within a selected user hive’s software configuration. The documented SystemCertificates child provides one verified facility beneath this vendor prefix. This layer narrows the software owner while leaving the feature unresolved; it is not itself a certificate store or a particular application. Keep the user-hive identity and next subsystem component when interpreting an access.

research.summary: Microsoft selects a vendor grouping within a selected user hive’s software configuration.
research.log_context: A record here concerns a Microsoft-owned configuration namespace in the resolved user hive. The subsystem child, operation and value data are necessary to identify its functional target.
cannot_infer: The ancestor does not identify a specific certificate or store.
The placeholder does not prove a particular user profile is loaded.
research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: The documented per-user certificate path establishes this ancestor.

definitions.explanation: SystemCertificates locates certificate system stores for the selected user hive. The parent identity determines which user context owns the location. Actual stores and certificate material are represented below it; the node is neither one certificate nor a guarantee of trusted status. Because system stores are logical collections, a registry view alone is insufficient to characterize every effective physical store or an application-specific chain-validation outcome.

research.summary: SystemCertificates locates certificate system stores for the selected user hive.
research.log_context: A user-certificate event needs the concrete hive, named store, certificate identifier and operation result.
cannot_infer: The template does not prove a user certificate exists.
The parent does not establish that a stored certificate is trusted or currently valid.
research.applicability: This describes the documented Windows registry namespace; available descendants and their behavior depend on the installed components and Windows release.

evidence.claim: User certificate stores use the user-hive SystemCertificates path.

relations.explanation: HKCC is the predefined alias of the current hardware-profile branch.
HKCR incorporates machine Classes registrations along with the applicable user Classes registrations.
HKCU maps to a concrete user branch represented by the UserHive schema; the template is not itself a runtime target.
An extension default value can name the ProgID represented by the ProgID schema.
When present, a CLSID subkey in a COM-oriented ProgID registration maps that textual identifier to a class; this is not a requirement for every Shell file-association ProgID.
A concrete class can associate with an AppID registration through its AppID metadata.
ProviderOrder names resolve to provider-specific registrations beneath Services.
Setup classes group installation configuration; interface classes describe exposed device functionality. These are distinct identities.
The WMI environment documentation separates system variables from per-user hive variables.
